title: Ethiopian Roasted Chickpea Snack
community: All of Ethiopia — the roasted chickpea snack
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Roasted Chickpea Snack — chickpeas soaked, dried, and dry-roasted until crunchy and golden. Part of the Qolo tradition (ETH018) — the dry-roasted snack eaten throughout the day, at church, at markets, and during coffee ceremonies.
longDesc: Roasted chickpeas are the legume component of the Ethiopian Qolo snack tradition — eaten alongside roasted barley, they form the complete snack that sustains Ethiopian daily life. Crunchy, nutty, and satisfying.
steps: Soak chickpeas overnight. Drain. Spread on a cloth. Dry thoroughly.
Heat a heavy dry pan over medium heat.
Add chickpeas. Roast, stirring constantly, for 20—25 minutes.
They should be golden, crunchy throughout, and nutty-smelling.
chefTips: Must be completely dry before roasting — wet chickpeas steam instead of roast.
Cool before eating — they crisp fully as they cool.
commonMistakes: Wet chickpeas — steam and become tough rather than crunchy.
cookingScience: See ETH018 for roasted grain and legume science. Chickpeas contain more protein than barley — producing more Maillard browning during dry roasting, which is why roasted chickpeas develop a deeper colour and more complex nutty flavour than roasted barley.
sustainabilityTips: Roasted chickpeas — zero packaging, no refrigeration needed, minimal processing.
healthBenefits: Low fat despite the satisfying crunch.
culturalNote: Roasted chickpeas are shared at Ethiopian coffee ceremonies, at churches, at market stalls, and between friends — they are the social snack of Ethiopian community life, always available, always welcome.
